about: The priest prays this portion of the Canon quietly, in communion with the Church. This form commemorates the most sacred day at the other Nativity Masses and throughout the octave, ending on January 1. After commemorating the saints, he asks the Father for His protection through Christ.

seg.tr: We are in communion and celebrate the most sacred day, on which blessed

ex.w001: The communion of the praying Church includes the commemoration of Mary and the saints whose names follow in this prayer.
ex.w005: The Savior’s birth is expressed through the image of Mary’s inviolate virginity bringing Him forth for the world. Mary remains the Mother named in the prayer.

seg.tr: Mary’s inviolate virginity brought forth the Savior for this world,

a.g: brought forth the Savior for this world

seg.tr: and we also venerate the memory, first of all, of the same glorious ever-Virgin

ex.w018: The memorial includes Mary, Joseph, the named Apostles and Martyrs, and all the saints. Their merits and prayers are invoked in the petition for God’s protection.

seg.tr: Mary, Mother of the same God and our Lord
and also of blessed Joseph, Spouse of the same Virgin,
and of Your blessed Apostles and Martyrs: Peter and Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon and Thaddeus;

a.g: of Your blessed Apostles and Martyrs

seg.tr: Linus, Cletus, Clement, Sixtus, Cornelius, Cyprian, Lawrence, Chrysogonus, John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian;
and of all Your saints. Through their merits and prayers, grant that in all things we may be defended by the help of Your protection.

a.g: we may be defended by the help of Your protection

seg.tr: Through the same Christ, our Lord. Amen.
